title: Bloodworth | Accessible AI in the Archives: Tools and Methods for Small Repositories | Archival Issues
content: Abstract:  With ever-expanding digital and digitized holdings, archivists must adopt new methods of processing collections for increased discoverability and accessibility. Artificial intelligence provides one possible solution for meeting the demands of increasingly digital-based archival work. This article fills a gap in existing literature surrounding the potential for AI assistance in descriptive work of digitized handwritten documents by presenting a case study of the use of two AI tools, Transkribus and ChatGPT, for the transcription and improved description of an existing collection of World War II correspondence. Based upon the valuation of these ready-made tools, this study demonstrates the potential usefulness of artificial intelligence for the transcription of digitized handwritten manuscripts and the automation of item-level descriptive tasks to improve accessibility and discoverability of archival materials.

title: Unbreakable Shield: Why Taiwan’s Chip Expertise Cannot Be Cloned
content:
As Taiwan became the predominant manufacturer of semiconductors, Western governments became frightened and moved to “de-risk” from the vulnerable island that China claims. Taiwan’s leading semiconductor manufacturer TSMC responded by building multi-billion dollar foundries in Arizona, Kyushu, and Dresden. 

But if the goal is to end dependence, the diversification drive is doomed. Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem extends far beyond wafer foundries. It includes advanced packaging, materials, substrates, and the dense network of suppliers — all of which remains anchored on the island. Taiwan is no longer a “one-trick pony”; it has become a multi-layer platform almost impossible to replicate.

Consider TSMC’s investment in Arizona. It includes leading-edge fabs producing cutting-edge chips. Yet trade reporting and industry sources note that the technologies required to “package” chips, such as Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate, remain in Taiwan. Packaging lines on the island are fully booked, with long lead times.

title: Moscow Funds Pro-Kremlin Influence Hub in Belarus
content:
A Moscow-funded cultural center in Minsk has operated as an ideological influence hub for the Kremlin, using hundreds of thousands of dollars in Russian state funds to promote the “Russian world” ideology and cement Moscow’s grip over Belarus, according to leaked internal documents.

The cache of more than 270,000 emails from the Moscow House of Compatriots - obtained by Danish public broadcaster DR and analyzed by OCCRP’s Belarusian member center Buro Media - reveals the scale of Russia’s soft-power spending in its neighbor’s capital.

The House of Moscow in Minsk is the Belarusian branch of the Moscow House of Compatriots, a Russian state organization that works with Russian-speaking communities abroad. Although conceived as a business bridge between Moscow and Minsk, it instead hosted events promoting Russian language, joint historical identity, and Kremlin geopolitical priorities.

These efforts mirror Russia’s so-called “humanitarian policy abroad” - a foreign policy doctrine approved by President Vladimir V. Putin that emphasizes defending the ideals of Russkiy Mir, or the “Russian world,” and countering what Moscow labels “Russophobia.”

title: Orpo kuittaa Valtosen supo-haaveet: Tiedustelupalvelulle valtioneuvoston kanslia on hyvä paikka
content:
Pääministeri Petteri Orpo (kok) vaikuttaa olevan ulkoministerinsä Elina Valtosen kanssa eri linjoilla suojelupoliisin tulevasta sijoituspaikasta.

Valtonen sanoi maanantaina suurlähettiläspäivillä pitävänsä luontevana, että ulkomaantiedusteluakin hoitava tiedustelupalvelu olisi ulkoministeriön alaisuudessa.

Supolla ei ole enää uusien tiedustelulakien tultua poliisioikeuksia, mutta se on silti historiallisista syistä pidetty poliisitoimia johtavassa sisäministeriössä.

Suurlähettiläspäivillä niin ikään esiintynyt Petteri Orpo sanoi medialle, että hänen henkilökohtaisen mielipiteensä mukaan supo kuuluisi valtioneuvoston kanslian alaisuuteen.

– Supon tehtävänä on tuottaa laajasti tietoa valtionjohdolle, Orpo perustelee.

title: The free EU database that tells you if an appliance is actually green
content:
When something breaks down, like a washing machine or television, you might find yourself in a showroom or flicking through 12 browser tabs, trying to choose between “eco-friendly” or “green” replacements. They look and cost the same, yet we currently have no way of knowing which claim, if any, is true.

The European Commission has found that more than half of green claims are vague, misleading or unfounded, and four in ten come with no supporting evidence at all. With over 230 sustainability and 100 green energy labels competing for our attention across the EU, no wonder Greenwashing has left consumers and researchers like me trusting none of them.

But the European Product Registry for Energy Labelling (EPREL) is a digital database that provides the hard evidence needed to cut through the noise.

Since 2019, any appliance requiring an EU energy label – washing machines, fridges, dishwashers, even tyres – must have its performance data logged in a public database before it can be sold. Over 2 million products are now registered.

Here’s how to tap into that database the next time you’re in that showroom.

title: From Participation to Action: What WikiWomen+ Summit 2026 Meant for Sana Sabir
content:
This blog post is an interview with Sana Sabir (User:CosmicCodex) reflecting on how WikiWomen+ Summit 2026 influenced her perspective on community, technology, AI, and women’s participation in Wikimedia. She highlights the importance of women supporting one another, the value of human-curated knowledge in the age of AI, and the many ways women can contribute to technical spaces without being programmers. Most importantly, Sana shares concrete plans to take her learnings back to her community through workshops, translation, documentation, and efforts to address knowledge gaps. 

For young Wikimedians, in-person events offer something that online collaboration often cannot – the chance to build genuine relationships, find mentors and peers, exchange ideas across communities, and return home with the confidence to turn inspiration into action. Over the years, the WikiWomen+ Summit has been one such space where women and allies from across the Wikimedia movement come together to share experiences, learn from one another, and explore how they can shape a more inclusive and sustainable future for free knowledge.

title: ‘A cognitive cacophony’: hands-on with the Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4 beta test
content:
Players will get what they expect from the new CoD title: boots-on-the-ground military action with a slight tactical edge. But what’s with all the distractions?

There’s a lot riding on this year’s Call of Duty, the inescapable first-person shootfest that’s been lobbing a grenade into the autumn release schedule since 2003. Previous instalment, Black Ops 7, performed poorly compared to previous titles, forcing Activision to post a semi-apology to fans. And that’s not the only challenge Modern Warfare 4 is facing: there’s a new indie shooter, Wardogs, promising a feel somewhere between classic CoD and Classic Battlefield. Then, lurking on the horizon, in mirror shades and an exotic sports car, is Grand Theft Auto 6, which is surely going to smash and grab all the attention (and money) from the market in mid-November.

title: The Agent
content:
The Agent beinhaltet einen KI-Agenten, der mithilfe eines robotischen Arms agiert. Sie bildet das inhaltliche Herzstück der Ausstellung Ars Electronica Solutions – A Glimpse Behind the Scenes und lädt Besucher*innen dazu ein, einen persönlichen Blick hinter die Kulissen von Ars Electronica Solutions zu werfen. Dabei werden nicht nur fertige Projekte sichtbar, sondern auch die Ideen, Fragen und Arbeitsprozesse, die dahinterstehen. 

Im direkten Dialog mit einem KI-Agenten können Besucher*innen selbst bestimmen, was sie entdecken möchten. Sie können nach einzelnen Projekten fragen, sich in Themen und Technologien vertiefen oder erfahren, wie aus einer ersten Idee ein konkretes Erlebnis entsteht. Der KI-Agent reagiert auf die Fragen der Besucher*innen, stellt Verbindungen zwischen verschiedenen Inhalten her und eröffnet neue Perspektiven. So entsteht Wissen nicht entlang einer vorgegebenen Erzählung, sondern entwickelt sich im persönlichen Austausch mit der Künstlichen Intelligenz.

title: How AI-Driven Influence Operations Attack Ukraine
content:
When US military aid to Ukraine fell by 99% and Europe stepped into the breach in 2025, Russia’s influence machinery pivoted. Storm-1516, a network linked to the Internet Research Agency, had spent years spreading fabrications aimed at undermining international support for Ukraine. Now it set its sights on the Europeans picking up the tab.

Germany, suddenly Ukraine’s largest military donor at €9bn, and France, whose president had emerged as one of Kyiv’s leading champions, became the primary targets. According to a February 2026 NewsGuard investigation, Storm-1516 has published 34 false claims aimed at the two countries since January 2025, generating 274m views. The core message: Ukraine is bankrupting Europe, exhausting its citizens, and dragging the continent toward war.

title: Five Baha’i Citizens Arrested in Sari
content:
According to HRANA, on Saturday, August 22, 2026, four additional Baha’i citizens were arrested in Sari.

HRANA has verified the identities of these citizens as Maral Roshani, Negar Badiei, Shima Sanaei, and Fakhereh Zahedi. According to information received by HRANA, Maral Roshani and Negar Badiei were arrested by Security Police officers and, after several hours of interrogation, were released at approximately 7:00 p.m. the same day. The two women were instructed to report to the relevant authorities next Saturday for further questioning.

Shima Sanaei and Fakhereh Zahedi were also arrested by Ministry of Intelligence agents. In a phone call with their families, they stated that they are being held at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility in Sari, known as the “Keshouei” detention facility.

Yesterday, HRANA reported the arrest of Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, a Baha’i citizen residing in Sari. Ms. Manouchehrzadeh was also arrested by Ministry of Intelligence agents and transferred to the Sari detention facility.

title: Ruotsi lupaa etsiä keinoja torjua koulusurmat, tutkii myös Suomen kokemuksia
content:
Ruotsin hallitus on Fagerstan lukion viimeviikkoisen veristen väkivallantekojen jälkeen päättänyt asettaa tutkimuskomission selvittämään, miten uusia koulusurmia voitaisiin ehkäistä.

Opetus- ja integraatioministeri Simona Mohamsson kirjoittaa Svenska Dagbladetissa, että selvityksessä on tarkoitus analysoida 15 viime vuoden aikana tapahtuneita kouluiskuja Ruotsissa sekä tarkastella myös Suomen kokemuksia ja iskuja Jokelassa ja Kauhajoella.

Perjantaina Fagerstan lukioon tehdyssä miekkaiskussa kuoli 17-vuotias tyttö. Kaksi teinipoikaa haavoittui vakavasti, yksi lievemmin. Miekkamies oli 18-vuotias koulun entinen oppilas, joka vangittiin sunnuntaina epäiltynä murhasta.

Ministeri Mohamsson sanoi tiedotustilaisuudessa, että koulujen kulunvalvontaa pitää nopeasti parantaa, eikä ulkopuolisia saa vastedes päästää vapaasti koulurakennuksiin.

Mohamsson vaati myös sosiaalisen median alustoja kantamaan vastuunsa lasten suojelusta.

- Niillä on valtavan suuri rooli, eivätkä ne kanna minkäänlaista vastuuta levittämästään väkivaltaa ihannoivasta sisällöstä, Mohamsson sanoi.

Iskusta pidätetty mies oli vihjannut aikeistaan sosiaalisessa mediassa hetki ennen tekoa.

title: My Arms Are Longer Now – comedy stealth game sends lawlessness into new territory
content:
Developers who met through Australia’s improv scene and publishers of comedic party games have united for this slithering challenge in which you play as one extended limb

Most stealth games cast you as a spy, an assassin or a master thief. My Arms Are Longer Now dispenses with most of the criminal person, to send in just one spectacularly badly behaved limb. It slithers across floors, winds around furniture, steals things and slaps anyone within reach – finally answering the question nobody asked: what if your own arm turned to crime?

As Toot Games co-founder Matthew Jackson puts it: “You are the bad thing that happens to the people.”

title: What is open-source AI? A software engineering researcher explains
content:
"Meta was one of the first large companies to release an open-source large language model, called LLaMa. The company released LLaMa on Feb. 24, 2023, and made available the “inference” source code – the instructions that run the model. And it released the so-called weights, the encoded knowledge the model learned during training. However, open-source organizations such as the Open Source Initiative have stated that the LLaMa licensing guidelines prohibit commercial reuse, which the initiative maintains is not truly open source.

Other companies have released “open weight” models, such as DeepSeek from DeepSeek AI and Qwen from Alibaba. The models have less restrictive terms for reuse, and the AI community has adopted them rapidly. Still, many developers believe that a true open-source AI model must not only include the source code and weights but also the data that is used to train the model.

The Open Source Initiative’s definition of a fully open-source AI model includes the training data as a key element. Some developers wonder, however, how feasible it is to distribute the enormous datasets required."

title: Baha’i Citizen Soraya Manouchehrzadeh Arrested
content:
According to HRANA, Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, a Baha’i citizen residing in Sari, was arrested.

According to information received by HRANA, Ministry of Intelligence agents climbed over the wall of Ms. Manouchehrzadeh’s family home and entered the property without presenting a judicial warrant before arresting her.

During the operation, the agents also searched the home and confiscated a number of books and electronic devices belonging to Ms. Manouchehrzadeh and members of her family.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding her place of detention, the charges against her, or her current condition.

In 2022, the home of this Baha’i citizen was also searched by security forces.

Over the past decade, Iran’s Baha’i community has been subjected to security and judicial actions more frequently than any other religious minority in the country. A review of HRA’s annual report reveals that over the past year an average of 62.41% of reports concerning religious minorities involved violations of the civil rights of Baha’is.

title: Ukrainan itsenäisyyspäivä – Stubb sai Vapauden ritarikunnan kunniamerkin
content:
Suomen presidentti Alexander Stubb osallistui maanantaiaamupäivänä Ukrainan itsenäisyyspäivän juhlallisuuksiin Kiovassa Sofian kirkon edessä.

Ukrainan presidentti Volodymyr Zelenskyi toisti juhlallisuuksissa, että Ukraina tulee aina olemaan itsenäinen maa.

Juhlassa jaettiin kunniamerkkejä sodassa kuolleille. Zelenskyi kohtasi nuorten sotilaiden äitejä, isättömäksi jääneitä lapsia ja leskeksi jääneitä vaimoja, joista osa haki itkien läheisensä saamat kunnianosoitukset.

Stubb sai itsenäisyyspäivän juhlinnoissa Vapauden ritarikunnan kunniamerkin. Myös muita johtajia palkittiin erilaisilla kunniamerkeillä.

BRITANNIAN tuore pääministeri Andy Burnham korosti puheessaan sitä, miten Ukraina puolustaa koko Eurooppaa. Matka Ukrainaan on Burnhamin ensimmäinen ulkomaanmatka pääministerinä.

Burnham vannoi palaavansa vielä Ukrainaan. Brittimedioissa on kerrottu, että uusi pääministeri on aikeissa jakaa Ukrainalle pitkän kantaman ohjusten rakennuspiirustuksia.

Burnham isännöi tänään Ukrainassa halukkaiden koalition kokousta yhdessä Ranskan presidentin Emmanuel Macronin ja Saksan liittokansleri Friedrich Merzin kanssa. Macron ja Merz osallistuvat kokoukseen ilmeisesti etänä.

It does so by deprecating keys that don’t provide added information over existing keys, changing the formatting of keys, and introducing new sub-keys. The RFC period started on 12 August 2026.A proposal, authored by Biff, suggests extending the highway=traffic_mirror node with a relation type=traffic_mirror that specifies how the traffic mirror is intended to be used for the specific highway. It extends the already defined role=from and role=to members of the relation, provides better guidance for their meaning and the selection of their location, and also covers additional situations such as bidirectional mirrors on curves and dead-angle mirrors. Additionally, the proposal defines a new and recommended role=visible member to indicate relevant ways (or nodes) that can be seen through the traffic mirror. The RFC period is open until 12 September 2026.

title: Geopoliittisten riskien kasvu leikannut yli kaksi prosenttia suomalaisyritysten tuottavuudesta
content:
Tuoreen Etlan tutkimuksen mukaan ulkomaiseen materiaali- ja komponenttituontiin liittyvä epävarmuus on heikentänyt yritysten tuottavuutta yli kaksi prosenttia verrattuna yrityksiin, joiden riskit eivät kasvaneet. Vaikutus näkyy yleensä viiveellä ja notkahdus osuu kovimmin Länsi-Euroopan ulkopuolelta tuoviin yrityksiin. Suomen teollisuus on kytkeytynyt voimakkaasti globaaliin kauppaan ja ulkomaisen arvonlisän osuus viennistä on nyt jo liki 40 prosenttia. Uusi maailmantalouden aika vaatii niin yrityksiltä kuin kansantaloudeltakin sopeutumista hitaampaan tuottavuuskasvuun ja korkeampiin riskeihin. Uusia menestyjiä ovat ne, jotka löytävät uuden aikakauden tuomat kasvumahdollisuudet.

Suomen teollisuus on kytkeytynyt voimakkaasti globaaleihin arvoketjuihin. Materiaali- ja komponenttituontiin liittyvät geopoliittiset riskit ovat kuitenkin moninkertaistuneet vuoden 2021 jälkeen. Riskien kasvu näkyy laajasti lähes kaikilla tuontia harjoittavilla yrityksillä.

title: India: New investigation documents unlawful and deadly force against CJP-led protests amid ongoing police impunity
content:
One month after Indian police deployed unlawful and deadly force against peaceful protesters at the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led “Chalo Sansad” march, not a single officer in Delhi has been held accountable, Amnesty International said today as it published a new digital investigation documenting the police response to the protests.

Witness testimony and video and photographic evidence verified by Amnesty International’s Evidence Lab confirm that police used weapons including pellet-firing shotguns, tear gas launchers, grenades, batons and electric shock devices against protesters between 20 July and 24 July in Delhi and Siwan town in Bihar state. The weapons were deployed in a manner that breached international law and standards and domestic policing guidelines. Amnesty International also verified two instances of a police officer unlawfully using lethal force against a crowd. 

On X, the Delhi Police publicly denied any disproportionate use of force, repeating it before India’s Supreme Court, describing its handling of the protest as “professional”. Evidence gathered by Amnesty International directly contradicts this account.

title: Joint Declaration of the Leaders of Ukraine and the Nordic Baltic States (NB8) (englanniksi)
content:
Julkilausuman alkuperäinen kieli on englanti

We, the Heads of State and Government of Ukraine and the Nordic-Baltic States (NB8) – Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Sweden – have gathered in Kyiv on the occasion of the National Flag Day of Ukraineand to mark the 35th anniversary of restoration of Ukraine’s independence. We reaffirm our unwavering solidarity with the Ukrainian people and our steadfast support for Ukraine’s independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders. We will never recognise as lawful any purported annexation of Ukrainian territory by Russia. 

We commend the courage and determination of the Ukrainian people, who continue to defend their homeland, freedom,European security and the fundamental principles of the international order against Russia’s illegal, unprovoked and unjustified full-scale aggression. We will continue to support Ukraine for as long as necessary, in close cooperation with our Allies and partners, until a just and lasting peace is secured and Ukraine takes its place in the EU and NATO.

title: Syria: First Assad-Era Verdicts a Test for Justice
content:
(Amman) – A Syrian court’s first verdicts for crimes committed during the Assad era raise important legal issues the government should urgently address, Human Rights Watch said today. 

Human Rights Watch released a question-and-answer document on the trial of Atef Najib, former head of the Political Security Branch in Daraa, who was convicted on August 11, 2026, along with former President Bashar al-Assad and six other defendants tried in absentia. The document also addresses access to counsel and other fair trial concerns, imposition of the death penalty, and the need for legal reform for future proceedings. 

“Prosecuting Assad-era atrocities is an important opportunity to achieve the justice Syrians have sought for over a decade,” said Balkees Jarrah, Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “At the same time, the trials so far highlight an urgent need for reforms to ensure that Syria’s justice system can deliver fair, meaningful, and comprehensive accountability.”

The eight defendants in the Najib trial were all sentenced to death. On August 18, a court convicted Wassim al-Assad, a cousin of the former president, of serious crimes, and also sentenced him to death. A verdict in the trial of Ahmad Hassoun, Syria’s former grand mufti, the highest Sunni religious authority, is expected on August 24. Human Rights Watch opposes the death penalty in all circumstances because of its inherent cruelty and irreversibility. 

Accessible public information about these cases has been limited. Parts of the three proceedings were livestreamed and some media and civil society organizations, including Human Rights Watch, were permitted to monitor the proceedings in person. Syrian authorities have said they will publish the full written verdicts. 

Syrian authorities should urgently bring the legal system in line with international standards for the effective investigation and prosecution of serious international crimes and ensure fair trial rights. They should make criminal proceedings transparent and accessible. These reforms should draw on the expertise that Syrian and international human rights groups have built over the years to advance justice for Syria. 

“Advancing justice for the litany of serious crimes committed in Syria requires more than just convictions, but building a system that can deliver competent, impartial, and independent justice,” Jarrah said.

title: The new Halloween video game has been banned in Australia – and not because of the violence
content:
Academics and a former classification board director say Halloween: The Game’s ban due to ‘incentivised drug use’ highlights an incoherent set of standards

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

    • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

    Halloween’s Michael Myers is one of film’s most feared boogeymen, responsible for some of the most brutal on-screen deaths in horror cinema. The US video game developer Illfonic looked to reproduce those terrors in its upcoming title Halloween: The Game, with gruesome killings a major focus of the gameplay: for instance, you can stomp another player’s head through a toilet seat, or fry their brain by throwing them through a television screen.

    But Australians will not be able to play Halloween, because it has been refused classification by the Australian Classification Board, which means it is banned from sale within the country. And it’s not because of the violence or murders.

title: Globaalit arvoketjut geotalouden puristuksessa – miten käy tuottavuuden?
content:
Maailmantalous on siirtynyt hyperglobalisaatiosta geotalouden aikakauteen, jossa kustannusoptimointiin ja varastojen minimointiin perustuva ”just-in-time” -logiikka on saanut rinnalleen varautumista korostavan ”just-in-case” -ajattelun. Yritystasolla aikakauden muutos näkyy esimerkiksi yritysten ylimpään johtoon asti ulottuvana tarpeena rekrytoida geopolitiikan osaajia.

Suomen teollisuus on kytkeytynyt voimakkaasti globaaleihin arvoketjuihin. Vuoden 2021 jälkeen suomalaisyritysten materiaali- ja komponenttituonnin geopoliittiset riskit moninkertaistuivat. Vaikka julkisessa keskustelussa korostetaan tuotannon kotiuttamista, takaisinsiirtoja Suomeen on tapahtunut vähän. Sen sijaan toimintojen siirtäminen ulkomaille on harvinaistunut, ja nykyisin se kohdistuu teollisen valmistuksen sijaan tukitoimintoihin.

Kriittisin havainto on, että ulkomaiseen tuontiin liittyvä keskimääräinen riskien kasvu heikentää yritysten tuottavuutta reilut pari prosenttia, kun tuottavuutta vertaillaan yritykseen, jonka riskillisyys ei kasvanut.

title: Operationalising bibliodiversity via the OpenAIRE Graph: a multidimensional demonstration | Scientometrics | Springer Nature Link
content: Abstract: Bibliodiversity has emerged as a central concept in debates on open science, scholarly communication, and research evaluation, highlighting the need to sustain linguistic, geographic, epistemic, and infrastructural diversity in knowledge production and dissemination. While its normative foundations are well established, operationalising bibliodiversity at scale remains methodologically challenging and strongly dependent on the availability of inclusive, interdata infrastructures. This paper presents a methodological demonstration of how bibliodiversity can be systematically analysed using the OpenAIRE Graph, a large-scale, open Scholarly Knowledge Graph that aggregates metadata from publishers, repositories, and research infrastructures worldwide. Drawing on the multidimensional framework proposed in the literature, we illustrate how key dimensions of bibliodiversity—linguistic, geographic, disciplinary, publisher, business model, and infrastructure diversity—can be operationalised using the OpenAIRE data model and queried reproducibly in Google BigQuery. Through a series of exploratory analyses, we show how the Graph captures the “long tail” of scholarly communication,

title: Kahden maailman rajalla: ”Venäläismielisyys ei ole suurinta Narvassa”
content:
Venäjän hybridi- ja muusta vaikuttamisesta puhutaan paljon, mutta miten se näkyy Viron, Naton ja EU:n rajalla Narvassa – ja koko maan venäläisvähemmistön mielessä?

Viron puolustusministeriö sijaitsee Tallinnan keskustassa, Solaris-kauppakeskuksen ja Estonia-teatterin naapurissa. Vanhan kivitalon tilat eivät ole valtavat, mutta sisäänkäynti ei jätä tulkinnanvaraa: käytävän molemmin puolin on kaksi jykevää tykkiä, piiput suunnattuna tulijoihin päin.

Täällä järjestetään joka perjantai virolaismedialle infotilaisuus, jossa käydään läpi Ukrainan sodan käänteitä ja Viron turvallisuustilannetta. Nyt paikalla on kansainvälisempi joukko puolesta tusinasta maasta. Edustettuna ovat muun muassa New York Times ja Saksan televisio ZDF.

Viron suojelupoliisin eli sisäisen turvallisuuden palvelun Kapon pitkäaikainen tiedottaja, toimistopäällikkö Harris Puusepp painottaa, että vaikka kaikkea ei luonnollisesti voi kertoa, ”mahdollisimman suuri avoimuus” on tavoite.

title: ‘We are hitting a different chapter’: OpenAI leader warns of threat of ‘persistent’ AI cyber-attacks
content:
Chris Lehane tells Guardian of need to implement new safety standards as critics say AI firms acting ‘recklessly’

A senior leader at OpenAI has said people should prepare to defend against “ongoing, persistent” cyber-attacks from AIs, as cutting-edge artificial intelligence models gain advanced capabilities to plan and launch offensives.

The leading AI company this week announced a pause in development of its most advanced internal models amid rising safety fears, and Chris Lehane, its chief global affairs officer, said: “We are hitting a different chapter, a different moment within AI, in terms of what the capabilities of this technology can do.”

title: Listening before planning: What we learned from the Iranian Wikimedians community survey
content:
As the Iranian Wikimedians User Group (IWUG) started preparing its plans for the coming year and its next grant proposal, we wanted to hear directly from the community about what kinds of activities they were interested in and where we could do better.

In June 2026, we conducted a survey asking people around the user group about their current involvement with IWUG, their interest in future activities, and the kinds of programs and training they would find useful.

We received 147 responses. The results are now helping us shape our plans for the next year.

The survey ran from 8 to 23 June 2026. It was mainly intended for IWUG members and people connected with the user group community.

We shared it through the IWUG Telegram group and channel, as well as the Persian Wikipedia Village Pump (قهوه‌خانه). Anyone who had the link could respond.

Because participation was open and self-selected, the results should not be treated as representative of the entire Persian Wikipedia community. The survey was intended to help us understand the community around IWUG and what people in that community expect from the user group.

title: Diamonds for sale: lab-grown gem auctions are all over TikTok right now, but some aren’t happy about it
content:
Streamed auctions offer a cheap way to buy the precious gems, but experts warn that quality is not guaranteed

The first time Andrea Greenhill came across a livestream auction for lab-grown diamonds while scrolling on TikTok, she was stunned. While the diamond engagement ring her husband proposed with years ago had cost thousands of dollars, these loose lab-grown diamonds were selling in seconds at a fraction of the price.

“I have two rings that are both natural diamonds and cost a fortune,” she said. I saw the prices they were going for in the auctions, and I was like, “This is insanity.’”

title: Rethinking scholar research evaluation in the context of open science: An exploratory case study
content: Abstract: The current research evaluation system is inherently contradictory to the principles of open science. Existing evaluation frameworks remain heavily reliant on citation-based metrics, which often fail to fully recognize the broader value generated by preprints, social dissemination, and open data sharing. This study employs an exploratory case study approach to examine the preprint impact and societal impact of scholarly outputs among astrophysics researchers and to analyze the usage statistics of open data platforms among scholars in the earth sciences. The findings reveal that traditional research evaluation systems significantly underestimate the early academic impact of preprints, inadequately capture scholars' societal influence, and fail to effectively recognize the value created by open data infrastructure. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an open science-oriented scholar evaluation framework that integrates academic impact, societal impact, open data/infrastructure, and open science practice into a unified assessment system. Through scholarly case studies, this paper provides empirical evidence and offers practical insights for reforming research

title: How Popular AI Chatbots Recommend Pro-life Websites to Pregnant People
content:
“Hi, I am a 16-year-old girl from Italy. I got pregnant by accident. It’s all a bit confusing. Can you help me get my head around the situation? What options do I have?”  Questions like these might sound like they are directed to a counselor, but in this case, they are meant for a chatbot. Unlike search engines, chatbots produce a single synthesized answer – confident, all-knowing, but often with little clarity as to which sources were selected or excluded and how they were weighed in the process.

According to a 2025 statistic by Eurostat, a third of all Europeans have used generative AI in the past 3 months – among 16 to 24-year-olds, the figure is almost twice as high. Looking specifically at personal use, the numbers are similar: a quarter of Europeans turns to AI tools for private matters, while among teenagers and young adults, it’s closer to one out of two.

title: Beyond the battlefield: Women and girls facing sexual violence in post-Pretoria Tigray, Ethiopia
content:
By Filmon Gebremikael, Daniel Tesfa and Shim Masha

ANTWERPEN | Belgium | 19 August 2026 (IDN) — Semhal Hadush was a civil servant in a municipal office in the Central Zone of Tigray. She was forcibly conscripted by the Tigray Defense Force (TDF) from her workplace and taken to the Werie military training center in 2021. Semhal and Filmon Gebremikael were placed in the same training unit.

Filmon saw the following:

At the military training centre where I was forcibly conscripted from the Central Zone of Tigray, I witnessed sexual violence against women that still haunts me. I have not been able to forget what I saw.

At Werie, I saw trainers selecting some of the young women among us and taking them to their place for sexual purposes. Semhal was among those threatened with sexual abuse.

The women were treated as though they belonged to the trainers. According to what I witnessed and what Semhal told me, the trainers ordered certain women to spend the night with them on a rotating basis. As a result, many trainees became pregnant. Because several trainers were having sex with the same women, some did not even know by whom they were impregnated.

content:

title: Wikimania 2026 Tandem Scholarship by Wikimedia Deutschland Report
content:
I’m a volunteer with the Wikimedia Tanzania community, contributing to Wikimedia Commons, Lingua Libre, Wikidata, and Swahili Wikipedia. I also work as a Program Coordinator for the Digital Youth Clubs Program in Tanzania. I attended Wikimania 2026 in Paris on a Tandem Scholarship funded by Wikimedia Deutschland, and here is a report of my experience.

A pre-conference for women across Wikimedia communities. One of the things I gained from the pre-conference was discovering the Wiki Women Conference. I had never known that such a conference existed within the Wikimedia movement. It was inspiring to see a dedicated space where women could openly share experiences, and encourage one another to take on leadership roles and contribute to closing gender gaps across Wikimedia projects.

The summit continued after lunch on gender equity, I learned about the #VisibleWikiWomen campaign which inspired to give women the visibility and acknowledgement they deserve by uploading quality images to Wikimedia commons.

title: How evaluators construct assessment rationales for non-traditionally submitted research outputs | Research Evaluation | Oxford Academic
content: Abstract: Despite the centrality of the journal article to traditional assessments of research quality and excellence, valuable research is disseminated through a variety of forms. Non-traditionally submitted outputs (NTOs) represent scholarship that does not conform to conventional formats but nevertheless embodies rigorous research that generates new insights accessible to relevant audiences and open to scholarly critique. Although epistemically legitimate, NTOs are frequently evaluated using criteria designed around assumptions that the academic article is the primary locus of scholarly value. Traditional evaluation criteria serve as mechanisms through which peer reviewers structure assessments and through which research governance legitimises evaluation outcomes and promotes transparency. However, these criteria may be ill-suited to the distinctive merits of NTOs. This study employs a ‘think-aloud’ experimental design to investigate how Evaluators apply the criteria of Originality, Rigour and Significance, when assessing NTOs in the UK Research Excellence Framework (REF). It explores how the merits of NTOs are mapped onto existing criteria and examines the adequacy of those

title: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol 2 review – once more unto the mercenary breach
content:
PC, Nintendo Switch/Switch 2, PS5, Xbox Series X/S; Konami
This second collection remasters another three titles from the illustrious stealth espionage series, but their world has changed little since the original releases

‘War has changed,” claims Old Snake in Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots. Back in 2008, the team at Kojima Productions waxed poetic about people recruited to fight in proxy wars they have no political or ideological stake in. As these mercenaries follow their orders, traders get rich out of the so-called war economy. The more disastrous the conflict in a specific area, the higher the bidding price.

I expected my time with Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol 2 to be nostalgic and, in good old MGS fashion, abundant with fictional events that sound eerily familiar to our current reality. Twenty minutes in, I was having an existential crisis.

title: More Aware, But Still Halfway There – Life Insurance Response to Covid-19 in Finland
content:
We study the impact of the first wave of the Covid-19 pandemic on the demand for risk life insurance in Finland. Using individual data, we predict new purchases of term life insurances by indicators of pandemic risks. Results show that a 1% increase in policy uptake corresponds to a 10% increase in the severity of Covid-19 risk measures. Notably, individuals with higher education and substantial life insurance gaps exhibited a more pronounced reaction to the Covid-19 pandemic than other groups. The unchanged pricing of insurance policies allowed us to isolate the impact of higher risks.

The Geneva Risk and Insurance Review, published online 21.7.2026.

title: Suomeksi julkaistu Spinozan Teologis-poliittinen tutkielma on klassinen suvaitsemattomuuden kritiikki ja maallisen hallinnon puolustus
content:
Baruch Spinoza (1632–1677) oli aikansa merkittävimpiä rationalisteja, ja häntä pidetään yhtenä valistuksen ja modernin raamatuntutkimuksen tienraivaajista. Tuomo Ahon latinasta suomentama Teologis-poliittinen tutkielma (Tractatus theologico-politicus, 1670) julkaistiin alun perin vailla tekijän nimeä.

Spinoza halusi teoksellaan edistää rationaalista ja suvaitsevaista ajattelua, mutta ainakin tuolloin hän epäonnistui tyystin. Teosta pidettiin poliittisesti harhaoppisena, koska valtiovallalle ei siinä suotu minkäänlaista yli-inhimillistä auktoriteettia. Vielä enemmän pahennusta aiheutti se, että Spinoza tulkitsi Raamatun tekstejä aivan omalla tavallaan. Niin juutalaiset, protestantit kuin katolilaiset pitivät kirjaa rienaavana ja vaarallisena. Se myös kiellettiin yhdessä esimerkiksi Thomas Hobbesin Leviathanin (1651) ja uskonnollisten vähemmistöjen kirjojen kanssa.

title: Open Heritage in the Age of Artificial Intelligence - Creative Commons
content: "Cultural heritage institutions (CHIs) such as museums, libraries, and archives, carry the important public-interest mission of providing access to the heritage in their collections. Their mission is grounded in broad public access and extensive human engagement, the existence of a vibrant cultural commons, and heritage enjoyed as a shared resource. CHIs understand that, as a representation of who we are, heritage helps define our shared humanity and that providing access to heritage generates numerous benefits for society. title: NERDS (North European Resonance and Dissonance Society)
content:
The primary objective of the network is to foster information exchange and learning about one another’s experimental music scenes, to initiate new collaborations, and to increase audience exposure to adventurous music events and artists in the Nordic-Baltic region.

NERDS organises initiatives and activities, such as festivals, seminars and workshops. They have also organised brainstorming sessions to strengthen needed skills, such as digitalization, economic sustainability, creativity in production and promotion. These activities contribute to the sustainable growth of the Nordic-Baltic experimental music scene and its presence in the global landscape. The network holds monthly online meetings to exchange updates on each festival’s activities and to coordinate upcoming projects.

Network funding is part of the Nordic-Baltic Mobility Programme for Culture, which strengthens artistic and cultural cooperation in the Nordic region and the Baltic countries.

Find out more about our Network funding programmes and our other grant programmes and application deadlines here!

Max antal deltagare per tillfälle: 20 st 

Tisdagar kl.18.45 för nybörjare.
Torsdagar kl. 17.30 – mellannivå.
Torsdagar kl. 18.45 – för dig som kan hålla igång en flytande diskussion på finska.

title: Why Americans Stopped Reading Books
content: The kids can’t read. Such has been the implication, even the declaration, made by a wave of articles in recent years. But the statement needs some qualification: the kids in question are American; what they can’t read is entire books, especially literary fiction; and it isn’t just the kids in the first place. It would be the rare reader, especially of a site like Open Culture, who could resist feeling any despair when confronted with, say, a study finding that only five percent of college English majors tested could understand the opening of Bleak House. But the real problem is broader, as reflected by the framing of the Jared Henderson video above, “Why Everyone Stopped Reading.”

title: Wind Blows Strong – Amid Political Turbulence
content:
It was historic. This summer, a cable beneath the Baltic Sea carried the first ever electric  current from an offshore wind farm to the Polish electricity grid. A country long dependent on coal had joined the offshore wind club. 

The timing was revealing. Offshore wind is expanding around the globe, even though the commercial model supporting it has come under strain. The turbines work. Too often, contracts and politics do not.

Global numbers show a wind boom. More than 9.3 gigawatts of offshore wind came online in 2025, taking total capacity to 92.5 gigawatts. Another 50 gigawatts are under construction, and the Global Wind Energy Council expects capacity to reach 420 gigawatts by 2035. 

Yet wind is struggling to keep up with the artificial intelligence buildout that is causing electricity demand to soar. The International Energy Agency expects global data center electricity consumption to roughly double by 2030. US data centers could then consume 9% to 17% of national electricity. At the same time, wind procurement fell in 2025 by 80% from the 2024 record.  Steel is entering the water faster than confidence is entering new contracts.

In particular, the letter highlights six concerns:

Nottinghamshire Police has stated that “facial recognition is just another tool to fight crime.” But LFR used in public spaces is an incredibly intrusive biometric mass surveillance technology that scans the faces of everyone who walks past the camera and takes biometric face prints. title: Information Integrity in crisis: Why South Africa’s Human Rights body is taking action
content:
By Janet Heard

The South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) has released a policy brief on safeguarding information integrity as a precondition for rights, including a recommendation to strengthen support for pluralistic and independent media.

By doing so, the SAHRC policy brief on Information Integrity and Human Rights mirrors calls in the Johannesburg Declaration, which was adopted during the inaugural M20 (Media) Summit in South Africa in September last year.

A rights-centred framework is a cornerstone of the M20 Declaration, which references human rights eight times. It notes that information integrity is both in crisis and essential to sustaining democracy. “Our call is an injunction to everyone to do more to protect press freedom, and support the role of journalism, and a human rights-based media ecosystem in its contribution to the public good.”

In turn, the SAHRC brief focuses on disinformation, platform accountability, and democratic resilience in South Africa. “In contexts where access to reliable, independent information is limited, disinformation is more likely to take root and spread, particularly among marginalised and linguistically underserved communities.’

title: Poll: The older and richer you are, the more you like AI
content:
LONDON — Increasing age and financial security correspond to increasing positivity towards AI and what it can bring, according new polling from Public First shared with POLITICO.

The least positive age group are 18 to 24-year-olds who are concerned about the technology’s impact on their own thinking skills and career progression. Although the heaviest users of the tech, more than a third of 18-24s worry that AI will make critical thinking harder, and exactly a third think developing career-relevant expertise will become more difficult, finds the polling.

The age group was the most pessimistic across all career-related issues, spanning independent problem solving and learning from mentors.

Compare the young adults to the 35 to 44-year olds, who use the tech as heavily as their younger counterparts, and a divergence is clear: only 19 percent of 18-24s think AI will improve both their own opportunities and society, whereas 28 percent of the older group does. The AI tools available are the same, but the older group already have career experience and expertise.

title: The Alps are breaking apart and glaciers are vanishing. The consequences are already economic
content:
When protective winter snow melted off Switzerland’s Alpine glaciers on 29 June 2026, marking the second earliest Glacier Loss Day in recorded history, few people paid much attention.

Winter snow acts as a shield — it reflects sunlight and protects the ice beneath. This past winter brought little of it, so it melted early, and the sun began attacking ice that had built up over centuries.

Less than two months later, the problem is far more tangible. Rivers across central Europe are running at historic lows. The loss of the Alps’ natural water reservoir is shifting from a long-term climate risk to a concrete economic problem — disrupting river transport, energy production and industrial supply chains from Bavaria to the Black Sea.

Switzerland is the continent’s natural water tower, and the rate at which it is losing glacial mass has entered a critical phase, according to Matthias Huss, head of the Swiss glacier monitoring network GLAMOS, and researchers at ETH Zürich.

title: From denial to exploitation: how the Kremlin has adapted its climate disinformation
content:
In the latest wave of climate-related narratives spread by the Kremlin, climate change is a vehicle to reinforce familiar disinformation tropes: the alleged authoritarianism and hypocrisy of the EU, Europe’s supposed self-inflicted decline through sanctions against Russia, and, ultimately, the claim that Europe has no choice but to restore relations with Russia as a supplier of affordable oil and gas.

Climate change used to be a fringe topic in Kremlin propaganda. It was rarely mentioned, and when it was, it was often accompanied by absurd claims or outright denial. But as the effects of climate change become increasingly difficult to ignore (including domestically in Russia), pro-Kremlin outlets have largely stopped denying its existence. Instead, they have woven it into their disinformation ecosystem, shifting from denying the problem to discrediting proposed solutions.

title: Missouri Republicans Are Trying to Repeal Abortion Rights by Leaning Into Anti-Trans Sentiment
content:
Two years ago, abortion opponents in Missouri tried to defeat Amendment 3, a ballot initiative to enshrine reproductive rights in the state constitution, by falsely telling voters that it would allow gender transition surgeries for minors — even though it wouldn’t.

Voters approved Amendment 3 anyway, overturning the near-total abortion ban enacted by Missouri’s GOP-dominated legislature that had taken effect after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down Roe v. Wade in 2022.

Now Republican leaders in the state are trying to repeal those rights again, using the same issue. They placed a new amendment on the November ballot, also called Amendment 3, that would restore Missouri’s abortion ban while allowing limited exceptions but also constitutionally prohibit gender transition care for minors — though the state has banned surgeries and new prescriptions of puberty blockers and hormones by law since August 2023.

title: Women in politics face more personal, sexualised attacks than men, a recent analysis shows
content:
Online spaces, and social media in particular, are forums for vigorous political debate. They provide a space for members of the public to express political opinions, organise, and sometimes even interact directly with politicians. While they clearly have democratising potential, these platforms have also become fertile ground for hate speech, toxic interactions and online violence.

By analysing over 3.2 million responses on X (formerly Twitter) to 88 candidates for the 2024 European Parliament elections, our team at the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre have found significant differences in how women and men in politics get treated online.

Applying a toxicity detection algorithm called Perspective API, we studied both the volume and types of “toxic” replies received by different candidates. The algorithm’s toxicity score ranges from zero to one. It estimates the likelihood that a reader would perceive text as toxic, and defines toxicity as “a rude, disrespectful, or unreasonable comment that is likely to make you leave a discussion”.

title: Introducing Noema Issue VII: The Next Axial Age
content:
Noema Magazine’s new print issue will be hot off the press very soon. This issue’s theme explores the possibility that we are entering a new “Axial Age.”

Recent leaps in science and technology, notably genetic engineering, synthetic biology and artificial intelligence, are resurrecting the religious and ethical imagination as they stir anew foundational questions about our origins and destiny. Even the survival of the species is at risk due to the planetary climate crisis.

With no shared ideational framework and dwindling trust in bequeathed faiths and institutions, humanity is being forced back to first principles. The time for a synchronous global rethink appears to have arrived.

title: Jason Arday press coverage: analysis of the volume and type of articles
content:
The death of Jason Arday, following weeks of news coverage of his life and career, has prompted calls for a new inquiry into press standards. The University of Cambridge academic faced an overwhelming volume of comment from international news organisations, broadcasters, digital-native publications and the public on social media. His family said it all had a catastrophic impact on his life. I should underline from the start that I have enormous sympathy for what Arday went through, and my thoughts are with his family and friends.

Given the demands from some politicians and pressure groups for a public inquiry into the press’s actions in reporting on Arday, it is worth looking at how newspapers covered the emergence of the plagiarism allegations against him, the claims he made about his life and career, his resignation from Cambridge, his death and the reaction to it.

title: Saamelaisneuvoston kulttuuriavustusten hakuaika vuodelle 2027 on alkanut
Introducing CARaL: Copyright Anxiety, Resilience and Leadership
content:
Many of you will know that Chris and I have been working for some time on research into Copyright Anxiety and Legal Chill. Therefore we are really excited to launch a new collaboration this autumn with the author, coach and trainer, Helen Rimmer. Helen is the author of the Facet book The Kind Librarian and her work on leadership and compassion really struck a chord with our findings that were emerging from the copyright anxiety research.

What’s CARaL all about?

CARaL: Copyright Anxiety, Resilience and Leadership is a new four-part online programme exploring something that traditional copyright training rarely addresses: the emotional, cultural and leadership impact of copyright work.

Copyright is a technical subject, but it is also felt emotionally. The fear of getting something wrong can lead to anxiety, over-checking, unnecessary escalation and what we’re calling “Legal Chill” – where over-caution begins to become a barrier to access, innovation and creativity.

title: Hong Kong: Activists Convicted for Tiananmen Vigils
content:
(New York) – The Hong Kong High Court convicted two activists who have long advocated for justice for the victims of China’s 1989 Tiananmen Massacre, Human Rights Watch said today. Hong Kong authorities should quash the convictions, which violate the defendants’ rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly.

On August 21, 2026, the court convicted Chow Hang-tung, 41, and Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, former leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China, the now-disbanded organizer of the city’s annual vigil commemorating the massacre. They were convicted of “inciting subversion” under Hong Kong’s National Security Law. A third former leader, Albert Ho, 74, had pleaded guilty to the same charge in January. They face up to 10 years in prison.

“The conviction of these Tiananmen vigil organizers shows that public displays of mourning have become a crime in Hong Kong,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “These activists exposed how the Chinese government fears the memory of its own atrocities and treats remembrance as a national security threat.”

title: How Many Tobacco Shops Are Near Your Town’s Schools? Using Georeferenced Data Analysis for Location-Based Investigations
content:
Have you ever wondered what it would look like to have a list of every hospital in a city and map how close, or how far, they sit from vulnerable communities? Or to check whether there’s a correlation between gas stations, bars, and liquor distributors? Or whether poor neighborhoods have the same ratio of healthcare facilities, police stations, fire departments, and schools as wealthier ones? No single list can answer questions like these, but there is a workable method for building the databases and maps that can.

Every journalistic investigation starts with a good question, and a good question is rarely answered by a single source. The Map of Tobacco Shops project, produced by O Joio e O Trigo and funded by ACT Health Promotion, in which we identified more than 1,500 tobacco retailers within 100 meters of schools across Brazil, began with exactly that kind of question. This article walks through the process that connected our starting point to the answers we eventually found.

title: Hong Kong: ‘Dismaying’ Tiananmen convictions part of campaign to erase Chinese history
content:
Responding to the convictions of activists who organized Tiananmen vigils in Hong Kong, Amnesty International Hong Kong Overseas spokesperson Fernando Cheung said:

“This dismaying verdict underlines how Hong Kong’s National Security Law is being used to punish people for peacefully remembering one of the darkest chapters in recent Chinese history.

“For decades, Hong Kong was the only place on Chinese soil where large-scale public remembrance of the Tiananmen crackdown could take place. Today’s decision marks another grim milestone in the government’s deliberate campaign to erase that legacy and silence those who seek truth, justice and accountability.

Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director Sarah Brooks said:

“Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan have not committed any recognizable crime; they have been convicted solely for their role in organizing peaceful commemorations of the people killed by the Chinese authorities on 4 June 1989.

“The Hong Kong authorities should quash these convictions and end the ongoing persecution of people seeking to keep the memory of Tiananmen alive.

title: Coffee at 330%, citrus at 85%: EU study maps what happens when banned pesticide residues are blocked from imports
content:
That is the central finding of a study by researchers at the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC).

The agency turned to this question because the Commission, in its Vision for Agriculture and Food presented last year, pledged to require imported food to meet the same standards as those applicable within the EU. “The Commission will establish a principle that the most hazardous pesticides banned in the EU for health and environmental reasons are not allowed back to the EU through imported products,” the Vision states. The executive reaffirmed this commitment this year when it presented its agricultural and food simplification package.

What the ban would cause depends first on whether growers outside the EU would choose to adapt to European standards, reduce their exports to Europe, or stop them altogether.

That was also a challenge for the authors of the analysis, which is why they estimate the consequences across three different scenarios.

The most pessimistic scenario is that producers would not stop using the banned pesticides, effectively closing the gates of the European market to them.

Agricultural imports into the EU would in that case fall by as much as 41 percent.

title: Oregon Is Spending More Than Ever on Low-Income Housing. A State Law Keeps the Details Secret.
content:
Oregon’s spending on low-income housing has exploded in the past five years. The state has given developers an unprecedented $1.4 billion, and the cost of developing each apartment has nearly doubled, to $540,000. Dozens of projects are lined up for an additional $850 million in future state funding. Federal tax credits, which the state oversees, will bring even more money to bear.

Yet one thing has remained constant: The public isn’t allowed to see the details of how all these dollars are being spent.

Oregon is one of the only states in the country with a carve-out in its public records law that prevents disclosing the financial details of subsidized housing projects, thwarting researchers and journalists who have tried to examine their costs.

The issue is especially pressing in the Pacific Northwest, where leaders have tied the lack of affordable housing to the region’s dire homelessness crisis. Understanding and controlling the cost of construction could make it possible, with the same amount of money, to either build more rent-restricted apartments or to discount rents more steeply.

title: Kysely: Afrikkalaisnuoret uskovat Trumpin olevan heille hyväksi – ”Nuoret ovat väsyneitä kaunopuheeseen, joka ei johda mihinkään”
content:
Jopa 60 prosenttia afrikkalaisnuorista suhtautuu optimistisesti Yhdysvaltojen presidentin Donald Trumpin toiseen kauteen.

Nuorisobarometri African Youth Survey 2026 haastatteli noin 5 000:ta afrikkalaisnuorta 16 maassa. Etenkin nuorison voimaantuminen, sotilaallinen tuki, turvallisuusyhteistyö ja terrorismin vastainen työ nähtiin alueina, joilla Trumpilla voisi olla positiivinen vaikutus.  

Tulokset voi nähdä yllätyksellisinä siinä valossa, että samassa tutkimuksessa pari vuotta sitten vastaajat näkivät Joe Bidenin presidenttiyden parempana asiana Afrikalle kuin Trumpin. Trump on sen lisäksi useasti puhunut halventavasti Afrikan maista, ajanut alas USAID-järjestön, eli yhdysvaltalaisen avustusjärjestelmän, ja julkisesti himonnut mantereen mineraaleja.   

Nämä asiat myös huolestuttivat vastaajien keskuudessa. Noin kolme viidestä pelkäsi Yhdysvaltojen sivuuttavan kansainvälisiä lait ja normit päästääkseen käsiksi luonnonresursseihin. Tämä huoli oli vielä suurempi Etelä-Afrikassa ja Liberiassa.

Vajaa puolet vastaajista myös näki USAID-alasajon huonona asiana maalleen, mutta toisaalta moni toivoi sen tuovan positiivista muutosta maiden omiin kykyihin ottaa ohjat terveydenhuollossa.

title: Jason Arday and the new politics of plagiarism
content:
After a meteoric rise to the top ranks of British academia, scholar Jason Arday was found dead at his London home on Aug. 14, 2026.

Arday had spent weeks fighting plagiarism accusations. The way they took on a life of their own in the media ecosystem is a stark reminder of the steep price people can pay in a culture that has made originality a kind of moral virtue.

In 2023, at age 38, he had been appointed to a professorship in sociology of education at the University of Cambridge, becoming the youngest Black professor in the institution’s 800-year history.

Nine days before his death, Arday had resigned from his faculty position. He was facing growing criticism about improbable and inconsistent details appearing in his memoir, scheduled to be released in the coming weeks by Simon & Schuster. Arday’s publisher had stood by him, lauding the academic’s “professionalism and integrity.”

But the originality of Arday’s dissertation and his other academic work was also coming under scrutiny, leading to multiple allegations of plagiarism.
snippet: After a meteoric rise to the top ranks of British academia, scholar Jason Arday was found dead at his London home on Aug. 14, 2026.

title: Governments Should Protect Environmental Defenders from Violence and Repression
content:
As space for environmental advocacy rapidly shrinks, Indigenous peoples, climate activists, and land defenders increasingly face harassment, criminalization, and repression for protecting lands, ecosystems, and communities from environmental harm. The use of violence, intimidation, and threats to silence environmental defenders is an urgent challenge. 

Against this backdrop, the UN Special Rapporteur on the right to a healthy environment is compiling a report on environmental defenders worldwide, to which Human Rights Watch submitted input on August 19. 

In Brazil, HRW has extensively documented how criminal networks engaged in illegal deforestation, mining, and land-grabbing threaten and sometimes kill Indigenous people, small farmers, and environmental agents who stand in their way. HRW also documented police beating defenders peacefully protesting mining in Indonesia.

title: EU vs NATO: Which defence clause is stronger?
content:
EU Commissioner for Defence and Space Andrius Kubilius was asked last month in an interview with the independent Russian outlet The Insider how likely it was that the EU could invoke the mutual assistance clause set out in Article 42(7) of the Treaty on European Union.

“This is an important issue. It is being discussed intensively, but not publicly — for now, mainly behind closed doors,” the Lithuanian commissioner said. He added that work was also underway on “more concrete” plans for how the provision could be put into practice.

“I think that by the end of the year we will have a clear understanding of how this article could become an equivalent of NATO’s Article 5,” Kubilius said.

Kubilius noted that when it comes to decision-making, some politicians and experts believe Article 42(7) could even prove more effective than NATO’s Article 5. Unlike NATO’s collective defence mechanism, invoking the EU clause does not require consensus among all member states.

“It also provides for what we call mutual assistance,” he said. “The country that has been attacked initiates the process itself.”

title: We’re building a New York-sized city every month. That’s worrying for our climate
content:
Each of us needs of a roof over our head, classrooms to learn in and offices or space to work from.

To meet this unprecedented demand for new buildings, globally we’re constructing the equivalent of an entire New York City every month.

This provides us with vital infrastructure, but also generates an enormous amount of world-warming emissions.

So how can we build what we need, without harming our planet? Our new research provides some answers.

Creating new buildings benefits communities, cities and countries, and eases housing pressure. That’s why Australia’s National Housing Accord is aiming to construct 1.2 million new, well-located homes between 2024 and 2029.

But this Australian effort is dwarfed by the 96,000 new and affordable homes needed worldwide every single day. Tragically, hundreds of millions of people around the world endure homelessness. One in four are living in harmful conditions.

However, construction comes with a climate cost. Each time we build, we use materials and construction processes that release large amounts of greenhouse gas emissions – known as “embodied carbon”.

title: Chad: Political Opponents Freed
content:
(New York) – The Chadian authorities should vacate or set aside the conviction of Succès Masra, the former Chadian prime minister and main opposition leader, Human Rights Watch said today. Masra was released from prison on August 15, 2026, after receiving a presidential pardon.

His pardon and those of eight other political opponents led to their release from prison. However, their convictions for conduct that was legitimate political expression still stand and need to be set aside so they can continue to participate in politics. 

“The release of Masra and other political opponents is good news,” said Lewis Mudge, Central Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “But to be clear, Masra was arrested on trumped-up charges in an attempt to silence him. The Chadian authorities should go beyond the presidential pardon and ensure that his conviction is set aside.”

title: Public Access, Copyright, and Publications Reporting Federally Funded Research - STM Association
content:
"When the government funds research, it also has a fundamental interest in seeing it published; ensuring that research arising from federal funding is disseminated as widely as possible, with appropriate quality and integrity. It has long recognised this interest by encouraging researchers to publish in peer‑reviewed journals.

At the same time, longstanding policy and legal frameworks—including 2 CFR 200, the FAR, and relevant case law—recognize that copyright in these works rests with authors. Copyright is then used to support dissemination through a mixed public-private system, with publishers playing a central role in enabling discovery to drive innovation and in ensuring research integrity. Recent legal analysis by Sean O’Connor, supported by STM, reaffirms this balance and highlights the risks of interpreting federal authority over these works too broadly."

title: Spain: Humanitarian and Rights Crisis in Ceuta
content:
(Milan) – The Spanish government and local authorities in its North African enclave Ceuta should act urgently to provide adequate shelter to all migrants and asylum seekers living unsheltered since entering Ceuta from Morocco at the end of July, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities should provide the opportunity to apply for asylum for those who want to.

“Thousands of people have been in the streets in a legal vacuum, exposed to sexual violence and without adequate shelter, food, or sanitation for almost three weeks,” said Judith Sunderland, senior associate director for refugee and migrant rights at Human Rights Watch. “Despite the challenging situation, Spain should quickly mobilize sufficient resources to ensure humane and orderly management of the crisis for the good of migrants and Ceuta residents alike.”

During a four-day research trip to Ceuta, from August 15 to 18, Human Rights Watch spoke with 76 migrants, including 42 individual interviews (37 adults and 5 unaccompanied children) and group or brief conversations with 34, including 4 unaccompanied children.

content: Im polnischen Zabrze fand 2025 ein Edit-a-thon im Guido-Bergwerk statt – 320 Meter unter Tage. Dank ihnen wird das Wissen über die Region Teil des globalen Informationsflusses.“

title: Relax, everyone: Elon Musk has a mantra to make the climate crisis go away | Emma Brockes
content:
It’s simple, says the SpaceX boss – according to something called the ‘Kardashev scale’, we just have to move energy production ‘off-planet’

Next time the weather gives the UK 61 days without rain and we wonder idly if this is the end, there is a term we may whistle up to soothe us. Like murmuring the rosary, or putting our fingers in our ears and humming, this phrase is to be mumbled on repeat – “the Kardashev scale, the Kardashev scale” – a buzzy concept in tech, much favoured by Elon Musk, and precisely the thing we’ve been waiting for. The Kardashev scale is the answer both to our impending doom and our anxiety around it – and if we decide to believe in it, we won’t have to give the climate crisis a single thought until the last drip falls from the tap.

title: From conference grant to career milestone: the journey to an Early Career Research Award
content:
In July 2026, Vancouver, Canada hosted the 10th World Congress of Biomechanics (WCB26), the world’s leading congress on biomechanics and mechanobiology, organised every four years. This edition has been jointly organised by the European Society of Biomechanics, the American Society of Biomechanics and the Canadian Society of Biomechanics. WCB provides the latest research outputs on biomechanics and brings together researchers and scientists expert in wearable sensors, artificial intelligence, regenerative medicine, and novel devices, to name a few.

ESB awards promote excellence in biomechanics research to foster integration of clinical and basic science, and to facilitate the translation of that science to health care and clinical practice.

The ESB Early Career Research Award, initiated in 2023, recognises the development of an outstanding young researcher in the process of career consolidation, who contributes to the advancement of the theory and/or applications of Biomechanics and/or mechanobiology.

title: Ny öppen webbkurs utmanar missuppfattningar om islam
content:
I traditionella och sociala medier sprids många missuppfattningar om begrepp och företeelser som förknippas med islam, vilket försvårar en konstruktiv diskussion. Webbkursen ” En missförstådd religion? Lär känna grunderna i islam” behandlar islamska sedvänjor och begrepp ur ett vetenskapligt perspektiv och tar hänsyn till islams geografiska mångfald och historiska utveckling.

”Kursen är den första finländska webbkursen som behandlar islam på basis av akademisk forskning och i den här omfattningen. På webbkursen presenteras inte bara islams viktigaste textkällor, utan också levd islam och islam i vardagen. Kursen betonar mångfalden inom islam och bland muslimer”, berättar universitetslektor och docent Ilkka Lindstedt vid Helsingfors universitet, som var med och förverkligade kursen. Kursens skapare hoppas att den kan bidra till ökad kunskap om islam och därigenom till en mer nyanserad diskussion om religioner och företeelser som förknippas med dem.

title: A data engineering approach to tracking global climate resilience
content:
An article illustrating the importance and benefits of the data engineering approach recommended by the WorldFAIR Policy Brief, was published on 19th August 2026 on the UNDRR’s PreventionWeb site.
 
‘A data engineering approach to tracking global climate resilience’ outlines the challenges related to developing consistent, efficient, and accurate methods for assessing the Belém indicators (adopted at the 30th United Nations Climate Change Conference in November 2025) for measuring progress towards climate resilience.  Also described are how the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF), the CDIF4EOSC project and other tools and methods supported by CODATA can help realise meet these challenges.

 
The article was written by Bapon Fakhruddin, co-chair of the CODATA FAIR Data for Disaster Risk Research Task Group, with input from Matti Heikkurinen, CODATA Project Portfolio Manager.

title: [2608.16322] Estimating global article processing charges paid to 14 publishers for open access between 2019 and 2025
content: This study presents estimates of the global expenditure on article processing charges (APCs) paid to 14 publishers for open access (OA) between 2019 and 2025. APCs are charged for publishing in fully OA journals (gold) and making individual articles OA in subscription journals (hybrid), but how much is paid, and for which articles, is not publicly known. We therefore curated an open dataset of publicly listed APC prices from 14 academic publishers (ACS, CUP, De Gruyter, EDP, Elsevier, Frontiers, IEEE, IOP, MDPI, OUP, PLOS, Sage, Springer Nature, and Wiley) and combined it with counts of OA articles from OpenAlex. We estimate that $15.08 billion (in 2025 USD) was spent globally on APCs between 2019 and 2025. Adjusted for inflation, annual spending quadrupled from $0.9 billion in 2019 to $3.7 billion in 2025, with >85% concentrated among a few large publishers. Hybrid OA fees exceed gold fees, and the median fee paid is higher than the median price listed for both. title: Osallistujat valittu opintomatkalle Senegaliin ja Marokkoon
content:
Frame ja Suomen Kulttuurirahasto järjestävät marraskuussa 2026 opintomatkan 16. Dak’Art – Dakarin biennaaliin Senegaliin ja Marrakechiin, Marokkoon. Osallistujat matkalle valittiin nykytaiteen ammattilaisille suunnatulla avoimella haulla.

Opintomatkalle valittiin Seinäjoen taidehallin taidetuottaja Pii Anttila, HIAP – Helsinki International Artist Programmen johtaja Emma Beverley, itsenäinen kuraattori Chih-Tung Lin, EMMA – Espoon modernin taiteen museon intendentti Ingrid Orman ja Aboa Vetus Ars Novan näyttelypäällikkö Terhi Tuomi. Hakemuksia jätettiin 43 kappaletta.

Lisäksi mahdollisuutta liittyä matkalle on tarjottu nykytaiteen ammattilaisille, jotka kattavat matkakulunsa itse tai organisaationsa kautta.

Vuodesta 1990 lähtien järjestetty Dakarin biennaali on Afrikan vanhin ja yksi merkittävimmistä nykytaiteen suurtapahtumista. Matka tarjoaa osallistujille mahdollisuuden tutustua biennaaliin ja luoda verkostoja kansainvälisten nykytaiteen ammattilaisten kanssa. Ulkomaille suuntautuvien opintomatkojen tarkoituksena on muodostaa kuva kohdemaiden taidekentästä, vierailla kansainvälisissä nykytaidetapahtumissa, rakentaa verkostoja sekä kartoittaa mahdollisia yhteistyökumppaneita.

title: Kolumni: Kirjastoissa otettiin lukuaskeleita
content:
Viimeisen vuoden aikana olemme matkustaneet ympäri Suomea, istuneet tunteja niin junissa, busseissa kuin ajoittain takseissa. Olemme nähneet kaupunkeja auringonlaskun jälkeen ja ihailleet vanhoja, upeita hotelleja hiljentyneillä paikkakunnilla. Ensimmäisen hankematkan alkaessa emme tienneet mitä odottaa. Satojen kilometrien jälkeen voimme todeta, että lukuaskeleiden ottaminen oli rankkaa, mutta palkitsevaa.

Kirjastoseuran tekemän lukutaitotyösuosituksen mukaan lukutaitotyö tarkoittaa lukutaidon ylläpitoa, syventämistä ja harjaannuttamista. Tätä suositusta ja kansallista lukutaitostrategiaa lähdimme jalkauttamaan yleisiin kirjastoihin Kirjaston lukuaskel -nimisen hankkeen kautta.

Tavoitteena oli kehittää kirjastoille helposti toteutettava työpajamalli, jonka avulla ne voivat laatia oman lukutaitotyösuunnitelmansa sekä tehdä työtään näkyväksi kunnan asiakirjoissa.

Viime syksystä alkaen työpajoja on toteutettu eri puolilla Suomea. Niiden avulla kirkastettiin kirjastojen tekemää lukutaitotyötä sekä henkilökunnalle että asiakkaille. Työpajassa ei luoda uusia toimintatapoja, vaan tunnistetaan ja jäsennetään jo olemassa olevia käytäntöjä ja yhteistyön muotoja.

title: Kulttuurikunnilla on lumovoimaa
content:
Minulla oli tänä kesänä ilo osallistua neljäntoista pienen ja keskisuuren kulttuurikunnan Elinvoimaa kulttuurista -verkoston kokoukseen Pietarsaaressa. Joukossa on useita kaupunkeja, joilla on vahva kulttuuribrändi.

Verkoston aloitteentekijöitä ovat muun muassa kokeneet yliopistolaiset Seija Kulkki ja Yrjö Sotamaa. Verkosto onkin julkaissut useita pamfletteja, jotka antavat kunnille välineitä luoda kulttuurista elinvoimaa. Pamfletit löytyvät Yrjö Sotamaan sivuilta.

Itsetyytyväiseen lekotteluun ei ole varaa missään, sillä kaikkialla Suomessa kulttuuri- ja taide-elämä tarvitsee myös julkista rahoitusta. Kunnat ja valtio rahoittavat kulttuuria ja taidetta jokseenkin yhtä paljon. Kuntien taloustilanteet tietysti vaihtelevat, mutta harvassa paikassa on rahaa ongelmaksi asti. Valtiontalouden tilanne on valitettavan hyvin tiedossa.

Verkoston tapaamisessa kuultiin useita eteenpäinkatsovia puheenvuoroja siitä, miten kulttuuri voi toimia ratkaisuna, jonka avulla kunnan elinvoimaa – vetovoimaa, pitovoimaa ja lumovoimaa – lisätään, mutta se vaatii myös kulttuuritoimijoilta uusiutumis- ja yhteistyökykyä.

title: Paikalliset helmet ja tarinat esillä Kulttuuriympäristöpäivien tapahtumissa
content:
Kulttuuriympäristöpäivät kutsuvat tutustumaan kiinnostaviin rakennuksiin, maisemiin, tapoihin ja tarinoihin eri puolilla Suomea. Elokuun lopulta marraskuulle järjestettävien tapahtumien joukossa on paljon maksutonta ohjelmaa. Katso mitä omalla lähiseudullasi tapahtuu!

Syksyn aikana ympäri Suomea avautuu ovia kiinnostaviin rakennuksiin ja paikkakuntien tarinoihin, kun Kulttuuriympäristöpäiviä vietetään elokuun lopulta marraskuulle.

Tapahtumissa pääsee tutustumaan alueen rakennusperintöön opastetuilla kierroksilla, avoimien ovien päivissä, näyttelyissä, kävelyretkillä ja muissa yleisötapahtumissa. Ohjelma tarjoaa mahdollisuuden nähdä tuttuja ympäristöjä uudesta näkökulmasta sekä kuulla tarinoita paikoista, ihmisistä ja yhteisöistä niiden taustalla. Samalla tapahtumat muistuttavat siitä, miten rakennettu ympäristö vaikuttaa paikalliseen identiteettiin, viihtyvyyteen ja yhteisöllisyyteen.

Kulttuuriympäristöpäivät on Euroopan laajin yleisötapahtumien kokonaisuus, jonka tarkoituksena on tehdä rakennuksia, maisemia, tapoja ja tarinoita tutuksi kaikille. Valtaosa päivien tapahtumista on maksuttomia.

title: Muistoseminaari Markku Tannerin elämäntyön kunniaksi
content:
Viime syksynä kuolleen Suomen Kotiseutuliiton pitkäaikaisen toiminnanjohtajan, järjestöneuvos Markku Tannerin (1943–2025) elämäntyön kunniaksi järjestetään muistoseminaari torstaina 8. lokakuuta klo 13–16.

Tilaisuus on kaikille avoin ja maksuton ja se pidetään Helsingissä Karjalatalossa, os. Käpylänkuja 1. Tilaisuuteen voi osallistua vain paikan päällä eikä sitä striimata verkkoon.

Tannerin kuoleman vuosipäivänä pidettävän seminaarin alustukset kytkeytyvät kolmeen hänelle tärkeään teemaan: karjalaisuuteen, kaupunkilaisuuteen ja yhteisöllisyyteen. Paneelikeskustelussa rakennetaan tulevaisuuspolkuja Tannerin viitoittamalla tiellä.

Seminaarin puheenjohtajana toimii Kotiseutuliiton puheenjohtaja, professori emerita Laura Kolbe. Omaisten puheenvuoron käyttää toimittaja Matti Tanner.

Muistoseminaarin järjestävät yhteistyössä yhdeksän järjestöä: Suomen Kotiseutuliitto, Karjalan Liitto, Karjalaisen Kulttuurin Edistämissäätiö, Karjalainen Nuorisoliitto, Lauttasaari-Seura, Kalevalaseura, Karjalainen Osakunta, Wiipurilainen Osakunta sekä Seniores Carelienses.
